picks.title: How Can You So Brazenly Insult Past Acharyas Of Vedanta
picks.summary: “Krishna is the Supreme Person, but at the same time He is beyond the knowledge of Brahman and Paramatma. The yogis and jnanis are confused in their attempts to understand Krishna, although the greatest of the impersonalists, Shripada Shankaracharya, has admitted in his Gita commentary that Krishna is the Supreme Personality of Godhead. But his followers do not accept Krishna as such, for it is very difficult to know Krishna, even though one has transcendental realization of impersonal Brahman.” (Shrila Prabhupada, Bhagavad-gita, 7.3 Purport)
picks.reason: Discusses Krishna's supreme nature and Vedanta interpretations on ultimate reality.

picks.title: How to Stop Letting People Affect You | Essence of the Geeta | Episode 81
picks.summary: Swami Swaroopananda, Global Head of Chinmaya Mission, is a revered spiritual leader known for his clear, profound Vedanta teachings. His wisdom guides many towards self-discovery and inner peace, making complex concepts accessible and inspiring globally. In this series, Swamiji distills the learnings from the Bhagavad Geeta and explains it in a way that allows everyone to enjoy the essence of the Geeta.
picks.reason: Swami Swaroopananda explains Bhagavad Gita's teachings on self-mastery and inner peace.

picks.title: 1813: The Philosopher vs the Mystic | Understanding the Passion of the Gopīs
picks.summary: To the philosopher, the weeping of Krishna's lovers looks like ordinary suffering. To the mystics it's the culmination of the highest knowledge. Evelyn Underhill — first woman to lecture in theology at Oxford — said the mystic speaks the disconcerting language of first-hand experience, something only really understood by another who has felt it. Raghunath and Kaustubha explore what it means to move from thinking to tasting — and why the passion of the gopīs is where all philosophy ends. Srimad Bhagavatam 10.39.8-26   ******************************************************************** LOVE THE
picks.reason: Analyzes the mystical passion of Krishna's devotees from Bhagavad Gita perspective.

picks.title: 1814: We Crash | God's Opulences and Our Limitations
picks.summary: What happens when an individual soul thinks the gifts they have are their own? Why do we see so many celebrities struggle, even though they have achieved so much success? Raghunath and Kaustubha explore the source of all opulences — beauty, strength, wealth, fame, knowledge, renunciation — and how when we receive even a touch of them we tend to think they are ours. And then the truth arrives. Crash.  Srimad Bhagavatam 10.39.25-31  Join Bhakti Recovery Retreat in Spain here: https://share.google/kShWGFuanwn4clArJ  ******************************************************************** LOVE THE POD
picks.reason: Explores Hindu ideas of divine gifts, ego, and spiritual crash from Srimad Bhagavatam.

picks.title: 🎚️  Embody Divinity
picks.summary:
Everyone seeks Divinity, but in Ch. 7, V. 16 of the Bhagavad Gita, Shri Krishna explains that the intensity and intention behind that search vary. Whether we turn to Divinity for relief, prosperity, or Peace, the deeper our understanding and devotion, the closer we move to embodying the Divine itself.

picks.reason: Explores embodying divinity through Bhagavad Gita's essential verses.

picks.title: The One With The Negotiation
picks.summary: “O scion of Bharata [Arjuna], O conquerer of the foe, all living entities are born into delusion, overcome by the dualities of desire and hate.” (Lord Krishna, Bhagavad-gita, 7.27)
picks.reason: Quotes Bhagavad Gita on human delusion and dualities, inviting reflection.

picks.title: I Know What To Do…So Why Dont I Do It? | Pujya Snehmunidas Swami | Windows Into Wisdom
picks.summary: Why do we know what is right, but still struggle to do it? In this episode of Windows into Wisdom by BAPS Better Living, we sit down with Pujya Snehmunidas Swami to explore one of the most honest struggles in spiritual growth: the gap between knowing better and actually doing better. Many of us have heard wisdom about patience, forgiveness, discipline, prayer, humility, and inner change. We may even feel inspired in the moment. But when life tests us, old habits, emotions, ego, and familiar patterns often take over. So how does wisdom move from something we admire to something we actually live
picks.reason: Explores the gap between knowing and doing in spiritual ethics.
